MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE
  Monday, June 6, 2022

1.  A regular meeting  of the  La Verne  City Council was called to order by Mayor Hepburn at 6:36 p. m.

2.  Councii Members  present:  Mayor Tim Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tem Muir Davis
  Council Member Robin Carder
  Council Member Wendy Lau
  Council Member Rick Crosby

  Absent:  None.

  Advisory personnel present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  Assistant to the City Manager JR Ranells
  City Attorney Robert L. Kress
  Assistant City Clerk Lupe Gaeta Estrella
  Community Development Director Eric Scherer

3.  Pledge of Allegiance  was led  by Mayor Hepburn.

4.  Announcements of Upcoming  Barbara Rugeley, Director of Observers of the League of Women Voters Mt.
  Communit Y Events  Baldy Area introduced Carrie Coolbaugh and Gwen Carr, the two new League
  Observers for the La Verne City Council.

  Sherry Best, President of the La Verne Historical Society reported on the
  Historical Society upcoming events and their fund raising efforts to restore
  Inman Conety 1938 International Truck.

  Julie Wheeler, Board Member of the Cultural Awareness and Social Inclusion
  Committee ( CASI), reported on the Committee' s mission that all are welcomed
  sex/ gender, sexual orientation,
  in the City of La Verne no matter their race,
  age, national origin/ ancestry,  religion,  etc.  She reported that they meet the
  first Wednesday  of the month  at 5: 00  p. m. and that the next meeting will be in-
  person.

  Thomas Allison, La Verne resident, reminded everyone to vote in the
  upcoming election on June 7, 2022 and that he is running for Judge.

  Council Member Carder introduced Rimmi Hundal the new Tri- City Mental
  Health Authority Director.

  Mayor Hepburn announced that two vote centers in La Verne were opened as
  of June 4,  2022, Veterans  Hall and St John Episcopal Church.

  items not listed in any other place on the agenda.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment.

  There were  public  comments  at  the meeting. ( To hear what was said during
  public comment, please visit the City' s website to view the archived Council
  meeting.)

8.  Council Comments  Council Member Carder stated that May was a very busy month with the many
  school  events going on. She congratulated the Bonita High School Girls
  Softball Team for wining CIF. She reported that the Memorial Day Ceremony
  was a beautiful event with the presentation of the Chair of Honor that was built
  by former Mayor pon Kendrick. She stated that Bagelry and Brew is under
  new  and  that she  attended  the Ribbon  Cutting.  She reminded
  ownership
  everyone to go out and Vote.

  Council Member Crosby reported that the Memorial Day Event was amazing
  so was the presentation of the Chair of Honor. He announced that Foothill
  Transit has a Class Pack Pass program for college students to help students
  to be more mobile and save on gas. He congratulated the high school
  graduates and the middle and elementary school students on their promotions.
  He stated he too had someone in his household who recently graduated. He
  stated that the last couple of weeks have been difficult with the passing of two
  former employees.

  Council Member Lau wished the Dads a Happy Father' s Day and
  congratulated all the graduates. She reported that she attended the University
  of  La Verne graduation  ceremony.  She reminded everyone to Vote and the
  County of Los Angeles is looking for Poll Workers. In addition, she asked that
  people consider donating to Sowing Seeds. She reported that June was Pride
  Month.  She reported that the University is hosting a Blood Drive on June 15,
  2022. She sent out her thoughts and prayers to the families of the recent
  passing of former Fire Chief Jankowski and former La Verne Information
  Systems Manager Bill Elftman.  She reminded everyone to take the time to be
  kind to each other.

  Mayor Pro Tem Davis also congratulated Bonita High School Girls' Softball
  Team for wining CIF. He reported that the Memorial Day Event was a beautiful
  observant and honor for the Military members who served and those who lost
  their lives.  He thanked La Verne resident Richard Bowen for reminding
  everyone of the importance of" D" Day. He reported on the La Verne/ San
  Dimas Educational Foundation and the Mental Wellness program offered by
  the Foundation.  He also reminded everyone to Vote.

  Mayor Hepburn mentioned the loss of two former employees in the last two
  weeks.  He also thanked La Verne resident Richard Bowen for reminding
  everyone of  the importance  of"  D"  Day. He reported he attended an Eagle
  Scout Ceremony, the Memorial Day Event, and Ramona' s Middle School
  promotion.  He reminded everyone to go out and vote and the vote centers
  close  at  8 p. m.
